So a gold re-mint under method_r29 needs the served silver replaced first, or a code change this order does not make.
chain_of_served_writes.which_silver_objects_change: daily_returns (44 rows in flow, 2 in return, every row in cash_leg and run_commit) and month_grades (1 row in computed_pct, every row in cash_leg and run_commit) change in content; account_day_value changes only in cash_leg and run_commit (every row of 21,102,041). commonwealth_fwd3_serve.py --apply (773-786) writes all three objects in one loop, so all three are replaced; there is no per-table flag. It refuses an existing object without --overwrite (781-782).
chain_of_served_writes.run_commit_point: A re-served silver object changes run_commit in EVERY row of all three tables (1,691,729 / 21,102,041 / 82,593) even where no number moves, and cash_leg from method_r28 to method_r29 in every row (the build takes the HEAD it runs at, serve lines 166-170). In the round-68 builds r28 and r29 share one run_commit (same HEAD), so that column did not differ between them; against the SERVED objects (run_commit 6f70d5cc01bb2e196266799a657be6d0b2dc8a16) it differs in every row.
chain_of_served_writes.local_build_path: None: the adapter cannot build from local tables (no argument, no function). The mapping of FWD-3 rows to day-file columns sits inline in build() (lines 459-493 and 541-561), not in a separable pure function; this measurement replicated it for the five data-dependent columns (market_value_eod, external_flow, total_return_daily, return_basis, day_quality) and controlled the replication against all 3,325 served day files.

Per day it writes data.parquet and manifest.json (emit_day 1881-1884). Their content would not change (sidecar symmetric difference 0; method_version 3 from sources.json).
